Note.Name: README
Note.Text:
## Overview

This repository contains the Forsta integration for Research Defender (RD). It
wraps both the client-side scripts that call the RD APIs and the server-side
logic that verifies responses and determines whether a respondent can continue
through the survey.

At a high level the integration:

- Collects RD Search V4 and RD Activity data into two Forsta text-list
  questions, `RD_Search` and `RD_Activity`.
- Validates and hashes RD Search data on the server before trusting the client
  payload.
- Retrieves RD Activity statistics server-side using an API token obtained in
  the browser.
- Aggregates the outcomes into a single-value question
  `research_defender_fail` where `0 = allow respondent to continue`,
  `1 = terminate respondent`.

## Configuration

The implementation is configured in the `consts` script. There are two steps
for configuration the project:

1. Fill in the `projectSettings` object (see comments for instructions)
2. Uncomment one of the template configs depending on the type of project.
   It is vital that this is set selected correctly because all of the termination
   logic depens on the values of this config. The defaults align with the company
   standard settings: 
   https://srcentre.sharepoint.com/:w:/s/AuditRiskandPrivacyCommittee/IQCcJahzDWdjRKFloXNC2qfeASJqFJQ_sPub2XwMWw4XtuQ?e=sUGs8X


## Data flow

1. Landing page (`client/onlineIntro.js`) unhides the intro content and the 
   next button only when RD calls finish. It listens for custom events fired by
   the producer scripts so the respondent cannot continue until responses are
   available.
2. **RD Search (`client/search.js`)** runs client-side, calls the RD Search V4
   endpoint, stores the raw payload and HTTP status into `RD_Search`, then fires
   the completion event.
3. **RD Activity token fetch (`client/activity.js`)** runs client-side, calls the
   RD Activity token endpoint, stores the raw token payload and HTTP status into
   `RD_Activity`, then fires its completion event.
4. **Server script (`rd.js`)** executes after the page submits. It parses and
   validates `RD_Search` via `processSearchResults()`, pulls statistics for
   `RD_Activity` via `processActivityResults()`, and finally computes
   `research_defender_fail` inside `determineOverallPassFail()`.

## Client-side behaviour

### search.js

- Uses `fetch` with credentials and an 8-second timeout supplied by Forsta macros
  (`^getTimeout()^`, `^makeRDSearchURL()^`).
- Writes `status_code` and `raw_response` to `RD_Search`.
- Emits a custom event (`^getSearchEventName()^`) so the intro screen can
  re-enable navigation.

### activity.js

- Calls the RD Activity token endpoint with the public API key. Response text
  goes into `RD_Activity.raw_token_response`, HTTP status into `status_code`.
- Emits a second custom event (`^getActivityEventName()^`) and unhides the intro
  once both events are received.

### onlineIntro.js

- Waits for both events (or detects prefilled hidden inputs) before restoring
  the original intro content and un-hiding buttons, preventing users from
  skipping the RD checks.

## Security considerations

The RD Search V4 endpoint supports signing the request URL with the private key
so Research Defender can confirm it was not tampered with. RD also signs the
response payload: `Validation.Surveys` and `Validation.Respondent` are hashes of
the corresponding entries in the `String` object. Because those string values are
not valid JSON, we extract key-value pairs via regular expressions to ensure the
data we trust matches what was signed. We should pursue a native, structured
response with RD to avoid depending on this workaround.

## HTTP status codes and timeouts

Both client scripts use an 8-second timeout. If a request does not complete in
time, it is aborted; the server interprets this as a failure since allowing the
respondent through would let malicious users block outbound traffic to bypass
screening. Every response captures the HTTP status code so we can differentiate
between network issues and valid RD denials.

Welcome to our survey!

The Australian Food Frequency Survey is conducted by the Social Research Centre, on behalf of the Australian Centre for Disease Control.

This survey will help us understand what foods Australians eat on a regular basis to help with investigating foodborne disease outbreaks and will ask about food consumption habits of children aged 14 years or under in the last seven days.

For this survey, your child must not have travelled overseas or experienced unusual sudden diarrhoea (three or more loose stools in 24 hours) or vomiting (two or more times in 24 hours) in the past week.

The survey will take approximately 20 minutes to complete, and your responses will be kept confidential.

If your child has experienced sudden diarrhoea or vomiting in the past week, Food Standards Australia New Zealand would like to ask you a small number of questions about your child's illness in an alternative survey. This will help us understand about illness from foodborne diseases.

It may take some people longer depending on their responses. Participation is completely voluntary, and you can stop or withdraw at any time. There will be no consequences for not completing the survey. If you don’t wish to answer any question, you can just click ‘Next’ to move to the next question.

The Social Research Centre acts in compliance with the National Privacy Principles. Your answers will be strictly confidential and no information collected in the survey will be used to identify you. The Australian Centre for Disease Control will not have access to individual identifiable information. Your answers will be combined with the information from other people completing the survey for analysis and reporting by the Australian Centre for Disease Control and the Social Research Centre.

If you have any questions about this survey or your participation in the survey, please call the Social Research Centre on 1800 023 040 or email at LifeInAus@srcentre.com.au.

The survey has been reviewed and approved by the Bellberry Ethics Committee (Ethics Number: 2025-04-599).

The Ethics Approval process requires you to be provided with a Participant Information Sheet.  In order to continue with the survey you need to first access this statement by clicking here.

For the ‘Next’ button to appear, please click on the link in the above sentence to read the Participant Information Sheet before continuing. The Participant Information Sheet will open in a new window. Once you have read the Participant Information Sheet, you will need to navigate back to this window to start the survey.

Welcome to the Gastroenteritis Survey. Since you said yes to experiencing sudden diarrhoea (3+ loose stools in 24 hours) or vomiting (2+ times in 24 hours) in the past 7 days that felt unusual for you, we would like to invite you to complete a short survey.

The Gastroenteritis Survey is conducted by the Social Research Centre, on behalf of Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ) and the Australian Centre for Disease Control.

By completing this survey, you will help us understand gastroenteritis (defined as 3+ loose stools and/or 2+ vomits in 24 hours).  For this survey, you must not have travelled overseas in the past week.

This survey will take approximately 5 minutes to complete, and your responses will be kept confidential. ^( f('preferred_incentive').get()!="Prefer not to receive reward" ) ? "To thank you for taking part in this survey, you will receive a $5 reward." : ""^

There will be no consequences for not completing the survey. If you do not wish to answer any question, you can just click ‘Next’ to move to the next question. 

The Social Research Centre acts in compliance with the National Privacy Principles. Your answers will be strictly confidential and no information collected in the survey will be used to identify you. FSANZ and the Australian Centre for Disease Control will not have access to individual identifiable information. Your answers will be combined with the information from other people who completed the survey, and will be used by FSANZ, the Australian Centre for Disease Control and the Social Research Centre for analysis and reporting.

If you have any questions about this survey or your participation in the survey, please call the Social Research Centre on 1800 023 040 or email at LifeInAus@srcentre.com.au.

FormText.Text:
Hello,
Welcome to the Gastroenteritis Survey. Since you said yes to your child who is going to have the next birthday experiencing sudden diarrhoea (3+ loose stools in 24 hours) or vomiting (2+ times in 24 hours) in the past 7 days that was unusual for them, we would like to invite you to complete a short survey about this.

The Gastroenteritis Survey is conducted by the Social Research Centre, on behalf of Food Standards Australia New Zealand (FSANZ) and the Australian Centre for Disease Control.

By completing this survey, you will help us understand gastroenteritis (defined as 3+ loose stools and/or 2+ vomits in 24 hours).. For this survey, your child must not have travelled overseas in the past week.

This survey will take approximately 5 minutes to complete, and your responses will be kept confidential. ^( f('preferred_incentive').get()!="Prefer not to receive reward" ) ? "To thank you for taking part in this survey, you will receive a $5 reward." : ""^

It may take some people longer to complete depending on their responses. Participation is completely voluntary, and you can stop or withdraw at any time. There will be no consequences for not completing the survey. If you do not wish to answer any question, you can just click ‘Next’ to move to the next question.

The Social Research Centre acts in compliance with the National Privacy Principles. Your answers will be strictly confidential and no information collected in the survey will be used to identify you. FSANZ and the Australian Centre for Disease Control will not have access to individual identifiable information. Your answers will be combined with the information from other people who completed the survey, and will be used by FSANZ, the Australian Centre for Disease Control and the Social Research Centre for analysis and reporting.

If you have any questions about this survey or your participation in the survey, please call the Social Research Centre on 1800 023 040 or email at LifeInAus@srcentre.com.au.

The survey has been reviewed and approved by the Bellberry Ethics Committee (Ethics Number: 2025-04-599).

The Ethics Approval process requires you to be provided with a Participant Information Sheet.  In order to continue with the survey you need to first access this statement by clicking here.

For the ‘next’ button to appear, please click on the link in the above sentence to read the Participant Information Sheet before continuing.

The Participant Information Sheet will open in a new window. Once you have read the Participant Information Sheet, you will need to navigate back to this window to start the survey.

To protect your privacy, before starting we need to check that you understand what is involved and agree to participate. 

Please read each of the following statements carefully. If you agree with all of the statements, select “yes” in the box below. If you disagree with any of the statements, select “no” in the box below.

  • I have read and understood the information in the Participant Information Sheet;
  • I understand I am being asked to provide consent to participate in this research project;
  • I understand the purposes of the research;
  • I provide my consent for the information collected about me to be used for the purpose of this research study only;
  • I understand that I am free to withdraw at any time during the project;
  • I understand that I can download a copy of the Participant Information Sheet from here;
  • I am aged 18 years or older
